title: Bauwaki language - Wikipedia
text: Bauwaki (Bawaki) is a Papuan language of New Guinea, sometimes classified as a member of the Mailuan family. It is 70% lexically similar to Abia of the Yareban family.

title: Music of Papua New Guinea - Wikipedia
text: The music of Papua New Guinea encompasses a wide range of traditional and contemporary styles developed across the country's highly diverse ethnic groups. Traditional celebrations known as sing-sing feature communal song and dance, and form a central part of cultural life.

title: Trans–New Guinea languages - Wikipedia
text: Trans–New Guinea is an extensive family of Papuan languages spoken on the island of New Guinea and neighboring islands, a region corresponding to the country Papua New Guinea as well as parts of Indonesia.

title: Bauwaki Language (BWK) – L1 & L2 Speakers, Status, Map ...
text: Bauwaki is a stable indigenous language of Papua New Guinea. It belongs to the Trans-New Guinea language family. Direct evidence is lacking, but the language is thought to be used as a first language by all in the ethnic community. It is not known to be taught in schools.
